title: From F1 driver salary to minimum wage: how to convert hourly to annual pay in Australia
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using 38-hour weeks, casual loading, and super. Includes F1 driver salary comparison and award rates from Fair Work Ombudsman.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, equating to $52,254.80 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate for each ordinary hour worked. If you enter your base rate into the timesheet, checking the casual loading box will add 25% before calculating annual pay. For example, a base rate of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour, and annual gross pay rises from $52,254.80 to $65,318.50 (assuming 38 hours per week). Super is then calculated on the loaded rate.

faqs.q: What is the super guarantee and how is it paid?
faqs.a: The super guarantee requires your employer to contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, on top of your salary. For 2026–27, contributions stop once your earnings exceed $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. Our calculator estimates super on ordinary earnings only, excluding overtime or bonuses.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to a fortnightly pay?
faqs.a: Fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For a full-time employee on 38 hours per week, weekly pay is hourly rate × 38. So fortnightly pay = hourly rate × 38 × 2. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, weekly pay is $1,004.72 and fortnightly pay is $2,009.44 before tax and super.

bodyMarkdown:
## From hourly to annual: the simple formula

Whether you're checking an **F1 driver salary** or your own award rate, the conversion from hourly to annual pay follows the same rule: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard is 38 hours per week under the Fair Work Act. That gives you:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for comparing job offers or understanding your [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).

### Why 38 hours?

The 38-hour week is the benchmark for full-time employment in most modern awards and the National Employment Standards. Part-time and casual employees may work fewer or irregular hours, so the calculator lets you adjust the weekly hours. For a quick estimate, 38 hours is the default.

## National Minimum Wage and award rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. That's a yearly gross of $52,254.80. But many employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the **Road Transport and Distribution Award 2020** has rates ranging from $26.87 per hour for a Transport Worker Grade 1 up to $31.55 per hour for Grade 10 (full-time). You can find your exact classification in the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual loading: 25% on top

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate for ordinary hours. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. On our [timesheet](/), you enter your base rate (the rate before loading), then check the box to add 25%. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For example, a casual Transport Worker Grade 1 would receive $26.87 + 25% = $33.59 per hour. The annual estimate then becomes $33.59 × 38 × 52 = $66,373.84 before super.

## Super is paid on top

Your employer must also contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into superannuation. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra cost to the employer. For 2026–27, the maximum contribution base is $270,830. So if your annual gross exceeds that, super stops at that threshold. Our calculator shows super as an additional amount, helping you see the total employment cost.

## Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. Remember that HELP debts, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included.

## Putting it all together: an example

Let's say you're offered a full-time job at **$30 per hour** (base rate). Your annual gross = $30 × 38 × 52 = **$59,280**. After tax (approx. $9,117) and Medicare ($1,185.60), your take-home is about **$48,977**. Your employer also pays super of $7,113.60 (12% of $59,280) into your fund. If you're casual, the base rate becomes $37.50 per hour with loading, annual gross = $74,100, and super = $8,892.

Even an **F1 driver salary** – rumoured to be in the millions – follows the same arithmetic, though their hours and contracts are far more complex. The principle remains: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 gives a baseline for comparison.

## Using the timesheet calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate, choose your weekly hours (default 38), and toggle casual loading. It then shows annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for award rates and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. For the most up-to-date award rates, always check the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog).

### A note on accuracy

This estimate is a guide only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
